title: dedicated-autoscaler-priority-scheduling-burst-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Aisha Khan
description: Motivation: Dedicated fleets occasionally experience priority-inversion under bursty traffic, which can cause SLA-sensitive customers to see degraded throughput even when overall capacity exists. This PR improves the Dedicated autoscaler by: 1) tightening priority-aware scheduling so high-priority tenants get guaranteed throughput under contention, 2) smoothing burst token-bucket behavior to avoid oscillatory scale-ups, and 3) adding richer utilization reporting and Prometheus metrics to enable SREs and customers to understand per-priority allocation and burst consumption. Summary of changes: - Implement priority-aware scheduling enforcement with a soft guarantee and configurable minimum throughput per-priority class. - Replace abrupt token-bucket refill with a leaky-smooth refill policy (tokenbucket_smoothing) to reduce local oscillation. - Add new metrics: dedicated_autoscaler_allocated_capacity{priority}, dedicated_autoscaler_burst_consumed_tokens{priority}, dedicated_autoscaler_queue_latency_p50/p95/p99{priority}, dedicated_autoscaler_scale_decision_reasons (labels). - Emit delta metrics for per-fleet and per-tenant utilization and a new reporting endpoint /internal/autoscaler/usage that returns summarized CSV for internal tooling (behind admin auth). - Update dashboards: autoscaler/fleet-priority-utilization and autoscaler/burst-consumption to reflect new labels and SLAs. - Tests: unit tests for scheduler and tokenbucket smoothing, and an integration test that replays a real traffic trace (trace/fleet_burst_trace_202602) to validate behavior. Backwards compatibility: all new behaviors are behind a new config flag dedicated.autoscaler.priority_guarantees.enabled (default true for new installs); tokenbucket smoothing is enabled by default but tunable via dedicated.autoscaler.tokenbucket.smoothing.alpha. No changes to client-facing API. Rollout plan: merge to main, deploy to staging (canary on 5% of Dedicated fleets), monitor new metrics for 48 hours, then ramp to 100% if stable. If regressions observed, we will toggle priority_guarantees.enabled=false as a kill switch. Related: builds on work in ENG-1106 (burst controls refactor) and addresses customer report SUP-4821.

review_comments: Daniel Kim (request changes): Can you add a short explanation of the soft guarantee math? I want to ensure we don't accidentally double-count tokens across priority classes.
Aisha Khan (reply): Added doc comment and unit tests that assert invariant under multi-priority workloads. See new tests in observability/metrics_test.go and pkg/autoscaler/scheduler_test.go.
Laura Chen (comment): CI failed on the first run due to a flake in the integration replay; reran and it's green now. Left a small nit about naming in tokenbucket.go.
Miguel Alvarez (approval): Verified performance on local perf-canary; p99 queue latency for high priority improved by ~35% in the synthetic trace. Approving for merge.
Release manager (comment): Please include a short release note and include rollout plan in the PR body.
release_notes: Enhancement: priority-aware scheduling and burst smoothing for Dedicated autoscaler. Adds new per-priority metrics and dashboards; configurable flags added for tuning. Improves high-priority throughput under bursty conditions and reduces oscillatory scale-ups.
